records.title: `docs_present()` ignores cite-only docs-backed trees
records.divergence_description: The startup warning path still treats cite-only documentation trees as docless even though the canonical documentation-state helpers classify the same trees as docs-backed.
records.documented_intent: REQ-001 requires plaintext files under `reference_docs/cite/` to count as valid documentation input on every startup path that decides whether the run is docs-backed or code-only.
records.code_behavior: `bin/run_playbook.py:1568-1574` only scans top-level files, while `_evaluate_documentation_state()` and `formal_docs_guard_banner()` recurse into `reference_docs/cite/` and accept cite-only trees (`bin/run_playbook.py:1617-1621`, `1666-1669`).
records.disposition_rationale: The divergence is entirely in the executable predicate used by the startup warning paths; the documented contract and the other code surfaces already agree on the intended cite-only behavior.
records.proposed_fix: Make `docs_present()` use the same recognized-plaintext predicate as `_evaluate_documentation_state()` and `formal_docs_guard_banner()`. See `quality/patches/BUG-001-fix.patch`.

records.title: `docs_present()` uses a broader predicate than the rest of the documentation-state logic
records.divergence_description: The warning helper counts README-only and binary-only trees as docs-present while also missing cite-only trees, so operator-visible startup messaging disagrees with the runner's stored documentation state.
records.documented_intent: REQ-002 requires warnings, state evaluation, and the formal-doc banner to share one recognized-plaintext rule across README-only, binary-only, cite-only, and top-level plaintext trees.
records.code_behavior: `bin/run_playbook.py:1568-1574` treats any non-dot top-level file as documentation, whereas `_reference_docs_plaintext()` filters to `.md`/`.txt`, skips `README.md`, and recurses into `cite/` (`bin/run_playbook.py:1583-1595`).
records.disposition_rationale: All three failing cells come from the same helper drift inside the startup warning path; no documentation or schema change is needed.
records.proposed_fix: Route `docs_present()` through `_reference_docs_plaintext()` or an equivalent shared helper so every documentation-state surface uses the same predicate. See `quality/patches/BUG-002-fix.patch`.
records.consolidation_rationale: A single predicate mismatch in `docs_present()` causes the README-only, binary-only, and cite-only parity failures.

records.title: Tier 4 ingest leaks nested non-`cite/` archives into Phase 1 context
records.divergence_description: The ingest pipeline treats every non-`cite/` plaintext file in the `reference_docs/` subtree as Tier 4 context, not just the documented top-level files.
records.documented_intent: REQ-003 requires Tier 4 ingest to stay limited to the documented top-level `reference_docs/` plaintext surface unless the contract is explicitly widened.
records.code_behavior: `bin/reference_docs_ingest.py:90-93` recursively enumerates the full tree, `_collect()` assigns `tier=4` to every non-`cite/` plaintext file (`189-227`), and `load_tier4_context()` returns those records directly (`263-276`).
records.disposition_rationale: The contract and the Phase 2 requirement are explicit about top-level-only Tier 4 scope; the bug is the missing filter in the ingest implementation.
records.proposed_fix: Restrict Tier 4 collection to top-level `reference_docs/*.{md,txt}` files while preserving `cite/` recursion for formal-doc ingest. See `quality/patches/BUG-003-fix.patch`.

records.title: Bootstrap mirroring drops the `cite/` formal-doc bucket
records.divergence_description: The bootstrap mirror helper preserves top-level plaintext docs but never copies the source-side `cite/` subtree into `reference_docs/cite/`.
records.documented_intent: REQ-004 requires bootstrap mirroring to preserve the top-level-vs-`cite/` placement semantics of the source bootstrap corpus.
records.code_behavior: `bin/bootstrap_self_audit_docs.py:50-61` creates `reference_docs/cite/` and then iterates only `SOURCE_DIR.iterdir()`, skipping subdirectories entirely.
records.disposition_rationale: The missing behavior is confined to the mirroring helper; the destination layout and the ingest contract already define the correct placement.
records.proposed_fix: Mirror both eligible top-level docs and eligible files under `docs_gathered/cite/` into the corresponding destination buckets. See `quality/patches/BUG-004-fix.patch`.

records.title: The Phase 1 validator accepts long placeholders instead of the written gate contract
records.divergence_description: The mechanical Phase 1 validator enforces only file existence, a 120-line minimum, and a generic findings regex even though the skill names a much stronger gate with exact headings and analytical minima.
records.documented_intent: REQ-005 requires the mechanical validator to reject `quality/EXPLORATION.md` artifacts that omit the exact mandatory sections and content depth named by the Phase 2 gate.
records.code_behavior: `bin/run_state_lib.py:171-198` stops after the line-count and generic findings checks, while `SKILL.md:1260-1273` defines the full required heading and content set.
records.disposition_rationale: The skill prose already defines the authoritative contract; the runtime validator is simply too weak and needs to enforce the documented checks.
records.proposed_fix: Extend `validate_phase_artifacts(..., 1)` to check the exact required headings and the Phase 2 gate's analytical minima before it returns success. See `quality/patches/BUG-005-fix.patch`.
records.consolidation_rationale: All absent cells are omitted by the same Phase 1 validation branch, so a single validator expansion closes the full missing gate contract.

records.title: Archive bug counting ignores canonical titled headings
records.divergence_description: Archive summaries split `BUGS.md` only on bare `### BUG-NNN` headings, so the canonical titled form `### BUG-NNN: Title` is silently skipped.
records.documented_intent: REQ-006 requires archive rendering to preserve bug counts from the canonical titled heading form used everywhere else in the playbook.
records.code_behavior: `bin/archive_lib.py:69` defines `_BUG_HEADING_PATTERN` without an optional title suffix, and `_extract_bug_counts()` depends on that pattern to segment the file (`321-338`).
records.disposition_rationale: The archive parser is the only outlier; the canonical heading form is already established by the rest of the protocol.
records.proposed_fix: Allow `_BUG_HEADING_PATTERN` to match an optional `: Title` suffix so canonical `BUGS.md` sections are counted. See `quality/patches/BUG-006-fix.patch`.

records.title: Mode A walkthrough has no quality/ archive step; Mode B always archives
records.divergence_description: Mode A re-runs silently overwrite the prior quality/ tree while Mode B unconditionally archives it to previous_runs/<ts>/, breaking the parity claim SKILL.md:62 makes.
records.documented_intent: SKILL.md:62 promises both modes use the same phase-prompt content; SKILL.md:122+150 advertise auto-archive as a contract guarantee.
records.code_behavior: bin/run_playbook.py:3829-3836 calls archive_run() unconditionally before Phase 1; SKILL.md:85-103 + phase_prompts/phase1.md contain ZERO archival guidance for Mode A; SKILL.md:154 tells Mode A operators to `git restore quality/` for recovery — implying delete-on-restart, not archive-on-restart.
records.disposition_rationale: Documented parity contract; Mode A archive guidance is the missing piece in SKILL.md / phase_prompts/phase1.md (either as prose or as an explicit pre-Phase-1 step).
records.proposed_fix: Add an archive step to the Mode A walkthrough (or document the asymmetry explicitly).

records.title: Phase 0 install-validator is mandatory in Mode A, absent from Mode B
records.divergence_description: SKILL.md:77 makes bin/qpb_validate.py a non-negotiable Phase 0 gate in Mode A (preventing the documented 2026-05-17 httpx install-path failure), but Mode B's bin/run_playbook.py never invokes the validator.
records.documented_intent: SKILL.md:77 calls Phase 0 install validation `non-negotiable; skipped/fabricated validation is the 2026-05-17 httpx/install-path root cause`.
records.code_behavior: grep `qpb_validate` in bin/run_playbook.py returns zero hits; Mode B runs its own pre-flight (sentinel files, source-edit baseline) but never invokes the install validator.
records.disposition_rationale: Mode B is the path most likely to hit install drift (CI/batch); the non-negotiable Phase 0 gate should be present in both modes.
records.proposed_fix: Invoke bin/qpb_validate.py from bin/run_playbook.py before Phase 1 archive_run().

records.title: WARN message at bin/run_playbook.py:1051-1062 lists 6 of 10 canonical install layouts
records.divergence_description: The operator-facing WARN enumerates 6 install layouts but SKILL.md:213-226, SKILL_FALLBACK_GUIDE, SKILL_INSTALL_LOCATIONS, and _GATE_INSTALL_LOCATIONS all carry 10. Missing from WARN: .codex/, .windsurf/, .cline/, .aider/.
records.documented_intent: Operator-facing WARN should enumerate the same canonical install layouts the resolver actually searches.
records.code_behavior: bin/run_playbook.py:1051-1062 lists 6 paths; the stale carry-over comment at line 1048 reads `list all 6 canonical install layouts — was 3 pre-fix` (predates the 6→10 expansion in instruction 046).
records.disposition_rationale: Operator-facing diagnostic that misrepresents supported layouts; recreates the failure mode v1.5.6 BUG-002 was supposed to close.
records.proposed_fix: Update the WARN message to enumerate all 10 canonical install layouts.

records.title: install_skill.py intro_short lists 4 of 8 auto-detected markers
records.divergence_description: intro_short at install_skill.py:786-791 says `auto-detection scans for the marker (.cursor/, .claude/, .github/, .continue/)` — 4 of 8 markers KNOWN_ENVIRONMENTS actually scans.
records.documented_intent: intro_short names the same markers detect_environment actually scans (KNOWN_ENVIRONMENTS — 8 markers at install_skill.py:46-58).
records.code_behavior: intro_short enumerates 4 markers; the visible installer message tells cline/windsurf/codex/aider adopters their tool isn't auto-detected, but it IS auto-detected.
records.disposition_rationale: Cosmetic/UX diagnostic but a documented contract drift inside the same file as the canonical list.
records.proposed_fix: Update intro_short to enumerate all 8 markers (or factor out a shared constant).

records.title: quality_gate.py::check_v1_5_0_index_md silently passes when summary is not a JSON object
records.divergence_description: The terminal gate emits PASS when INDEX.md `summary` is present but not a dict (e.g., a string, null, list); the validator FAILs the same input. schemas.md:1128 requires `summary | object | yes`.
records.documented_intent: schemas.md:1128 declares summary type `object`, required `yes`; both gate and validator must enforce.
records.code_behavior: quality_gate.py:2858-2866 reads `if isinstance(summary, dict):` before the required-keys loop; a non-dict summary skips the check and the function ends with pass_; bin/validate_phase_artifacts.py:366-369 has an explicit FAIL for the same input.
records.disposition_rationale: The gate is the terminal authority and carries weaker enforcement than the validator on the same schema field.
records.proposed_fix: Add a FAIL branch in quality_gate.py:2858-2866 when summary exists but is not a dict.

records.title: 089c three-state verdict has no gate_verdict enum value in schemas.md / validator / INDEX.md
records.divergence_description: v1.5.7 089c added a third gate verdict state (GATE PASSED WITH CLEANUP NEEDED) but schemas.md §11 and validate_phase_artifacts.py still enforce the three-value enum {pass, partial, fail} — different three. No defined mapping for the new state.
records.documented_intent: Auditor verdict taxonomy is three-state (PASS, PASS WITH CLEANUP NEEDED, FAIL) per phase_prompts/phase6.md:48-52 + phase_prompts/phase6_auditor.md:73-82; the persisted gate_verdict should capture the same distinction.
records.code_behavior: quality_gate.py:230-235 emits three verdicts; schemas.md:1130 specifies enum {pass, fail, partial}; bin/validate_phase_artifacts.py:109 enforces ('pass', 'partial', 'fail'); SKILL.md:209 still says `(pass / partial / fail)` — operator-facing prose drift.
records.disposition_rationale: The 089c contract update is incomplete — the schema/validator/INDEX/prose surfaces were not updated in lockstep with the gate.
records.proposed_fix: Add `pass_with_cleanup` to schemas.md §11 enum + _INDEX_VALID_VERDICTS + update SKILL.md:209 + document the mapping from `RESULT: GATE PASSED WITH CLEANUP NEEDED` → `pass_with_cleanup` in archive_lib.

records.title: archive_lib._GATE_RESULT_PATTERN regex cannot match the v1.5.7 gate output format
records.divergence_description: _GATE_RESULT_PATTERN searches for `gate_result: 'PASS'` style key=value text that the v1.5.7 gate never emits. archive_lib.py:73's regex returns no matches; _extract_gate_verdict falls through to PROGRESS.md substring match or returns 'unknown'.
records.documented_intent: Mode B's archive_run() parses the actual gate output to populate INDEX.md summary.gate_verdict with one of pass/fail/partial.
records.code_behavior: bin/archive_lib.py:73 defines `_GATE_RESULT_PATTERN = re.compile(r"gate_result['\"]?\s*[:=]\s*['\"](PASS|FAIL|WARN)['\"]?")`; the actual gate output is `RESULT: GATE PASSED|FAILED|...` (quality_gate.py:210-234). Zero matches of `gate_result` token in quality_gate.py.
records.disposition_rationale: End-to-end break: Mode B archive writes gate_verdict='unknown' which then fails the validator's enum on otherwise-successful runs.
records.proposed_fix: Update _GATE_RESULT_PATTERN to match `RESULT: GATE (PASSED|FAILED|PASSED WITH CLEANUP NEEDED)` and map to the schema enum (after BUG-012 schema fix).

records.title: Validator requires schema_version: '2.0' literal; gate's case-4 fallback says missing is OK
records.divergence_description: An INDEX.md missing schema_version passes the gate (case-4 fallback at quality_gate.py:2821-2829) and fails the validator (literal-match at validate_phase_artifacts.py:350-356) — opposite enforcement direction.
records.documented_intent: Gate and validator agree on whether an absent schema_version is acceptable on a current Phase 5/6 run; validator runs as a strict subset of the gate per validate_phase_artifacts.py:42-48.
records.code_behavior: Gate's case 4 treats absent schema_version as a v1.5.4 stub (PASS); validator's _check_index_v2_fields requires literal `'2.0'` (FAIL).
records.disposition_rationale: Documented subset claim is broken in this direction.
records.proposed_fix: Pick one canonical behavior: either tighten gate case-4 to FAIL on absent or relax validator to accept absent on stub-INDEX shape.

records.title: phase_prompts/phase6_auditor.md has no Mode-B branch despite phase6.md routing Mode B to it
records.divergence_description: phase6.md:5-7 routes a Mode B subprocess to honor the same witness contract as the auditor, but phase6_auditor.md's text declares 'You did NOT execute Phases 1-5' — directly contradicting Mode B reality.
records.documented_intent: SKILL.md:62 claims both modes use the same phase prompt content; phase6.md branches on Mode A vs B but routes both to the same witness contract.
records.code_behavior: phase6_auditor.md:1-15 asserts the auditor did not execute prior phases; phase6_auditor.md:16-30 forbids writing new artifacts — incompatible with a Mode B subprocess that just executed Phases 1-5 in-line.
records.disposition_rationale: Prompt content drift: phase6.md acknowledges Mode B's identity but the auditor prompt does not.
records.proposed_fix: Add a Mode-A vs Mode-B branch at the top of phase6_auditor.md mirroring phase6.md:5-7.

records.title: _REFERENCE_DOCS_PLAINTEXT_EXTS omits .rst; cite-only .rst trees misclassified as code-only
records.divergence_description: A repo with only reference_docs/cite/virtio.rst is ingested by reference_docs_ingest (which accepts .rst per SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS) but classified as code-only by all three startup surfaces (docs_present, _evaluate_documentation_state, formal_docs_guard_banner) because _REFERENCE_DOCS_PLAINTEXT_EXTS = {'.txt', '.md'}.
records.documented_intent: REQ-001 requires plaintext under reference_docs/cite/ to count as documentation on every startup path; SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS includes .rst per instruction 060/A-12.
records.code_behavior: bin/run_playbook.py:2021 defines _REFERENCE_DOCS_PLAINTEXT_EXTS without .rst; bin/reference_docs_ingest.py:76 includes .rst in SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS.
records.disposition_rationale: The BUG-001 fix closed .md/.txt but left .rst (a first-class plaintext extension) open — the SAME failure-mode shape on a different extension.
records.proposed_fix: Extend _REFERENCE_DOCS_PLAINTEXT_EXTS to {'.txt', '.md', '.rst'} mirroring SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS.

records.title: Cross-surface predicate parity drift between _reference_docs_plaintext and _iter_candidates extension sets
records.divergence_description: _reference_docs_plaintext()'s docstring at bin/run_playbook.py:2028-2040 PROMISES mirror parity with _iter_candidates(), but the extension sets diverge on .rst.
records.documented_intent: REQ-002 COS 4: the three helper surfaces agree with the ingest pipeline they mirror.
records.code_behavior: Same root cause as BUG-016; the docstring claim is structurally broken.
records.disposition_rationale: Consolidates with BUG-016 — one-line shared fix.
records.proposed_fix: Same fix as BUG-016 (extend the extension set).
records.consolidation_rationale: Same root cause + one-line fix as BUG-016, but covers REQ-002 (cross-surface agreement) rather than REQ-001 (cite-only classification).

records.title: Bootstrap mirror silently drops .rst plaintext from docs_gathered/
records.divergence_description: bin.bootstrap_self_audit_docs.PLAINTEXT_EXTENSIONS = {'.md', '.txt'} silently drops docs_gathered/cite/*.rst; the post-mirror self-audit has nothing for ingest to find on .rst-only spec trees.
records.documented_intent: REQ-004: bootstrap mirrors both top-level and cite/ sources preserving placement; every plaintext file ingest would later read.
records.code_behavior: bin/bootstrap_self_audit_docs.py:35 PLAINTEXT_EXTENSIONS = {'.md', '.txt'}; bin/reference_docs_ingest.py:76 SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS includes '.rst'.
records.disposition_rationale: Compounds with BUG-016/017: even fixing the startup surfaces leaves the bootstrap step as the data-loss gate. Recommend a shared constant.
records.proposed_fix: Change PLAINTEXT_EXTENSIONS to {'.md', '.txt', '.rst'} and factor out a shared module-level constant.

records.title: Phase 1 validator enforces only ~half of the documented 12-check gate
records.divergence_description: The Phase 1 validator at bin/run_state_lib.py:294-470 implements roughly 6 of the 12 checks documented in references/phase1_exploration_guide.md:692-704. Missing enforcements: Derived Requirements section (check 3), multi-module finding spread (check 4 second half), Quality Risks content depth (check 6), pattern-matrix coverage (check 7).
records.documented_intent: REQ-005: mechanical validation aligns with the stronger Phase 2 entry gate documented in the exploration guide.
records.code_behavior: Validator checks file existence, ≥120 lines, basic heading presence, ≥8 findings with file:line citations, and a 3-4 FULL-pattern count — but skips the four checks named above. A shallow but heading-conformant artifact still passes.
records.disposition_rationale: The contract REQ-005 names is structurally broken — the BUG-005 fix tightened the gate but not to the documented strength.
records.proposed_fix: Add `Derived Requirements` heading + REQ-NNN regex check; add distinct-modules spread check on file:line citations; harden matrix check to verify FULL+SKIP row count matches canonical pattern count.

records.title: Terminal gate's _BUG_HEADING_RE only matches digit-only IDs; archive and validator accept alphanumeric+hyphen
records.divergence_description: The gate's _BUG_HEADING_RE = r'^###\s+BUG-(\d+):' only matches digit-only BUG IDs; archive_lib and run_state_lib both accept alphanumeric+hyphen IDs. Future iteration-suffixed IDs (e.g., BUG-007-PARITY) would be silently invisible to the gate's cardinality / consolidation_rationale checks.
records.documented_intent: REQ-006: every consumer of BUGS.md headings sees the same set of bugs.
records.code_behavior: quality_gate.py:286 _BUG_HEADING_RE digit-only; archive_lib.py:69 _BUG_HEADING_PATTERN accepts [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]*; run_state_lib.py:586-589 matching form.
records.disposition_rationale: Cross-module consistency: three regex variants of the same construct.
records.proposed_fix: Widen _BUG_HEADING_RE to match archive_lib.py:69. Add a cross-module consistency test pinning all three regexes.
